claims.text: Equimolar polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength despite favorable ductility.
Dynamic recovery is the predominant cause of the relatively low hardness and strength of equimolar polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi.
Grain boundaries facilitate dynamic recovery in polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi.
Removing grain boundaries by using nearly defect-free single crystals will suppress dynamic recovery.
Suppressing dynamic recovery in single-crystal CoCrFeNiTi will increase its yield strength relative to polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi under similar deformation conditions.
Suppressing dynamic recovery will alter the strain-hardening behavior of single-crystal CoCrFeNiTi.
Grain boundaries in polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi act as sinks for dislocations.
Grain boundaries in polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi act as sources for dislocations.
Grain-boundary-mediated dislocation activity promotes dynamic recovery and limits hardening in polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi.
The absence of grain boundaries in single crystals leads to greater intrinsic dislocation accumulation.
Greater dislocation accumulation in single-crystal CoCrFeNiTi produces higher resistance to deformation.
Single-crystal CoCrFeNiTi will show fewer recovery-related dislocation rearrangements than polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi.
As-cast equimolar polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi has moderate hardness, lower compressive strength, and favorable plasticity.
The favorable plasticity of as-cast equimolar polycrystalline CoCrFeNiTi is caused by extensive grain-boundary-mediated dynamic recovery.
The proposed mechanism applies to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state under compression at 25 °C and 600 °C.
